entities.name: NOX2
observations: In isolated rat and mouse ventricular myocytes, Ang II-induced ROS and cellular arrhythmia susceptibility were absent with gp91phox/NOX2 deficiency.
Independent atrial evidence found Ang II-triggered ROS, Ca2+ overload, and arrhythmic events were suppressed by NOX2 deficiency or inhibition.

entities.name: Angiotensin II
observations: Ang II increased NOX2-dependent ROS and cellular arrhythmia-related phenotypes in ventricular myocytes.
Ang II induced atrial ROS, Ca2+ overload, and arrhythmic events in a NOX2-dependent manner.

entities.name: PKA
observations: In the key ventricular study, PKA inhibition abolished Ang II-induced increases in peak ICa and INa in a NOX2-dependent setting.
Redox-dead PKARIα prevented Ang II-induced ICa stimulation, supporting redox-sensitive PKA control, although NOX2 and arrhythmia were not independently tested in that study.

entities.name: CaMKII
observations: Ang II-induced diastolic SR Ca2+ leak and the associated pro-arrhythmic phenotype required CaMKIIδ in the key NOX2 study.
NOX2-mediated CaMKII oxidation is also reported in hyperglycemia-induced proarrhythmia, but that evidence is indirect for Ang II.

entities.name: PMID:25073061
observations: Primary study in isolated rat and mouse ventricular myocytes: NOX2 deficiency prevented Ang II-dependent ROS and cellular arrhythmia susceptibility; PKA and CaMKII affected distinct pro-arrhythmic branches.

entities.name: PMID:29625277
observations: In Pak1-deficient atrial myocytes and AF models, Ang II-triggered arrhythmic Ca2+ overload was suppressed by NOX2 deficiency/inhibition and NCX inhibition; PKA and CaMKII were not directly tested.

entities.name: PMID:33483749
observations: NOX2 overexpression modestly increased AF inducibility in vivo but did not consistently alter RyR2 leak or PKA/CaMKII-mediated RyR2 phosphorylation, indicating context dependence.

entities.name: PMID:34583520
observations: Ang II-induced ICa stimulation required redox-sensitive PKARIα/PKA, but the study did not isolate NOX2 or measure arrhythmia.

entities.name: PMID:33926209
observations: NOX2-mediated CaMKII oxidation was reported in hyperglycemia-induced proarrhythmia, not in an Ang II intervention; this is indirect evidence for the present question.
